notes.title: Nvidia left the rally on read
body: Green market. Red Nvidia. Awkward when you’re usually the reason the screen is green. On Sunday, Nvidia’s board said it was opening an independent investigation after reports that CEO Jensen Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort. The board said it had no reason to think company secrets or national security were compromised. By Monday morning, the wider market was up and Nvidia was down.

Last week had its own mess. Stocks cheered after the midterms. Then Thursday showed up. The Nasdaq dropped 5.5%, and SOXX, the chip-stock fund, dropped 12.15%. After Democrats won, investors worried new data centers could face more pushback over permits and power bills. A GPU can write you a breakup text in seven languages. It still can’t get the zoning board to call you back. If the building slips, the boxes meant to go inside it can ship later.

Nvidia actually lost less than the chip fund last week. Down 8.8% for Nvidia, down 13.1% for the fund. Nobody’s putting that on a trophy, but it matters. Thursday had a whole group of chip stocks selling off together. Monday had Nvidia going red while the wider market bounced. That’s when the board news gets its own tab. The stock chart can show me the split. It can’t tell me how much of the drop belongs to the investigation.

I get the temptation to call every red candle a sale. I also get the temptation to text an ex because they changed their profile picture. In both cases, I’d like one more piece of evidence. If customers are pushing back deliveries, show me the dates. If Nvidia is shipping on time but waiting longer to get paid, show me the cash. And if the other chip names start sliding again too, I’m looking back at the whole group before I pin everything on Nvidia.

There’s a real difference between a customer saying, “We’ll take the chips in March instead,” and an investor saying, “What if they take the chips in March instead?” One can move money out of this quarter. The other can move the share price before anybody has changed an order. If you hear about a real delay, look for the project name and the date. That’s the part I can check next quarter.

Nvidia reports Nov. 17. I want two updates. What has the board learned? And are customers moving delivery dates? Until I see something on either one, the chart gets one tab and the receipts get another. Yes, I have too many tabs. These are the ones paying rent.

performance.window: Five sessions through Nov. 6, 2026 · close to close

notes.flowRemark: Friday’s options trades didn’t time travel. I’m watching whether people are still paying to protect against a drop after the headline.
